title: Lazy kernel swap + attention-window trim causes KV memory aliasing and subtle logits drift
creator: Riley Chen
description: Summary: After landing the lazy kernel swap optimization that defers fused-attention -> fallback transitions until workload boundaries, we are seeing a class of correctness failures in production for long-sequence tracing workloads where attention-window trimming is enabled. Symptoms include token-level shifts (predicted token indices off by +1 in a reproducible subset), small but reproducible logit deltas leading to downstream sampling divergence, and occasional transient OOMs on fallback kernels. This ticket tracks investigation, short-term mitigations, and a fix path.
observed_behavior: 1) Deterministic token offset for some prompt seeds (token at position N becomes token at N+1). 2) Logit differences of magnitude 1e-3 to 1e-2 between baseline and optimized builds for identical inputs after kernel swap boundary. 3) Sporadic KV read/write alignment faults detected in sanitizer traces and occasional CUDA memory warnings (non-fatal) when fallbacks are hot-swapped under load.
expected_behavior: Kernel selection changes must be transparent to model outputs. No token shifts, and logits should match baseline floats within pre-existing FP tolerance thresholds (e.g., < 1e-6 relative on stable eval set). No memory aliasing or alignment-related warnings.
reproduction_steps: Environment: runtime-2.4.0-optim-lazyswap build + CUDA 12.2 + Amp-FP16 enabled
Run against baseline: checkout runtime-2.3.7-stable and run same command; compare tokens and logits with diff_tool.py
Trigger with synthetic microbench: python perf_tests/trace_swap_stress.py --switch-at-step 128 --trials 1000
Enable sanitizer logs: export REDWOOD_KV_SANITIZER=1 and capture runtime logs for trials that show divergence
hypothesis_root_cause: When attention-window trimming reduces the effective KV width, the deferred kernel swap path does an in-place remap of KV buffers assuming identical stride/tiling between fused and fallback kernels. Under some memory layouts the trimmed window produces a non-canonical stride; the lazy swap code rebinds pointers without re-padding the destination slab which creates aliasing between subsequent KV slots. The aliasing manifests as shifted reads during the next decode step. Additionally, the fallback kernel uses a different accumulator order (fp16 accumulate -> fp32 cast) causing the small numeric drift observed once aliasing corrupts a few lanes.
mitigation_plan: Hotfix: disable lazy-swap when attention trimming is enabled (config flag) - immediate rollout to affected customers
Add runtime guard: new invariant checker that validates KV slab stride and non-overlap before performing an in-place kernel pointer rebind
Add sanitizer: extend REDWOOD_KV_SANITIZER to detect overlapping ranges and fail fast
Rollback candidate: revert lazy swap merge if hotspots continue after guard rollout
action_items: Asha: Write and ship config gate to disable lazy-swap when attention-trim != 0 (ETA 1d) (PR #3482)
Riley: Implement and unit test KV non-overlap validator in kernel_selector (ETA 2d)
Ben: Add sanitizer checks and integrate into CI (ETA 3d)
QA: Add fuzz test case for trimmed window + swap sequences to perf harness (ETA 4d)
Eng-Review: design microbenchmark to stress stride mismatches across GPUs (RTX-A5000, A100, H100)
priority_rationale: High customer impact for long-context customers (observed in 3 paying clusters), produces incorrect outputs and rare OOMs—classed as P0 until hotfix is rolled
acceptance_criteria: 1) Hotfix gate deployed and rolled to all affected regions (no further incidents in last 48h)
2) KV non-overlap validator has unit and integration tests and is enabled in CI
3) Repro harness runs 10k trials without token shifts on runtime-2.4.0 with lazy-swap enabled + validator
4) Root cause PR merged with kernel stride fix or safe copy semantics (no in-place aliasing)
notes: This regression surfaced after an optimization to reduce copies during kernel transitions. The perf win is valuable, but correctness must come first—we need a rigorous validation of memory layouts when performing pointer rebinds. Consider adding a small alignment/pad policy to ensure canonical stride for trimmed windows.
